stemBlocks.value: The vector a is the column vector with components 6 and 8. (a) Calculate |a|, the magnitude of a. (b) Write down a unit vector in the direction of a.
Think first: The two components are the legs of a right-angled triangle whose hypotenuse is the magnitude.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p178-q02 from workbook page 178.

solutionSteps.instruction: Divide the vector by its magnitude.

strategyBlocks.value: Apply Pythagoras to the components for the magnitude, then divide the vector by that magnitude to get the unit vector.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) |a| = 10  (b) the unit vector is (1/10)(6, 8) = (0.6, 0.8), that is the column vector with components 3/5 and 4/5

whyThisWorks.value: A column vector describes a horizontal step and a vertical step, which meet at a right angle, so its length is exactly the hypotenuse Pythagoras gives. Dividing every component by that length scales the arrow down to length 1 without turning it, so the direction is preserved while the size becomes the standard unit — which is why a unit vector is the pure statement of direction.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding the components to get 14 instead of using Pythagoras.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting the square root and giving |a| = 100.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing only one component by the magnitude.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing only one component by the magnitude.

examTip.value: Always verify a unit vector by squaring and adding its components — the total must be exactly 1.
